routing.reason: One optional field across a small stack (new migration, validation in the API, one form field and display, tests, README) with fully specified acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow — a normal feature with a plan and review, not an urgent fix — cost if wrong: none, hotfix would only skip the plan gate

Ruling: skip the product-owner frame step — the six acceptance criteria are already testable and complete (format, null/clear semantics, exact 400 message, migration, UI, tests/docs) — cost if wrong: a missed edge case such as validating due_date on POST when it is not a string, caught by the code review

Ruling: no PM, architect, UX, SEO steps — a small change with an existing add form and list, no design decision, no public page metadata — cost if wrong: the date field's look may need a revision after the visual review

Ruling: leave the migrations review (dba) on as the workflow defines — a new migration adds a column to the existing tasks table, and it must be appended to the migrations array in src/db.ts, never editing the shipped one — cost if wrong: a bad migration breaks existing databases

Ruling: security review at medium effort — user input is parsed and validated (strict YYYY-MM-DD with a real-calendar check, rendered into the page, so it must be escaped, not injected as HTML) but there is no auth, payment or personal data — cost if wrong: a validation or output-encoding hole goes unnoticed
Ruling: no squads declared, so the lead plans the whole ticket (back for src/db.ts, src/tasks.ts, src/app.ts and tests; front for public/; docs for README) — cost if wrong: none
Ruling: budget $1.50 — a small S change with a handful of agent steps — cost if wrong: the run stops at the cap and asks for more

criteria.why: Task and Row gain due_date: string|null, SELECT * returns it, column is nullable so default is null; tested on POST, GET and list.
POST passes optional due_date (undefined→null); PATCH uses `"due_date" in changes` so absent keeps, null clears; tested.

isValidDueDate checks regex plus a round-trip through Date, which rejects 2026-02-30 and non-strings. It runs before any write and returns the exact error message. Tests cover bad formats, a non-leap Feb 29, a number, {} and "".
ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN is appended as a new migration, so old rows get NULL. A test starts from a version-1 DB and checks this.
A <time class="due"> element renders next to the title when due_date is set, and the form has an <input type=date>; the POST payload includes it only when filled.
New API and migration tests were added and the README documents the field, the PATCH semantics and the error. The UI has no test, which is acceptable here.

findings.what: The test imports `migrate` from ../src/db.ts, but the diff doesn't show db.ts exporting it. If it isn't already exported, the whole test file fails to load.
The edit `const filter =document.querySelector(...)` drops a space and is unrelated whitespace noise on a line the ticket doesn't touch.
The try/catch added to the submit handler is not strictly in the ticket. It is justified, because the new 400 would otherwise be an unhandled rejection, but it is a small extra change.
PATCH validates due_date before checking that the task exists. An invalid date on a missing id returns 400 instead of 404. This is defensible but untested.
`"due_date" in body` throws a TypeError if the JSON body is null or a primitive. `body.title` already fails the same way before it, so the problem is not new.
The `changes` object is built with a long inline type, and `"due_date" in changes` is re-checked in tasks.ts. The logic is duplicated but small.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion with a small, correct implementation: strict date validation, PATCH set/keep/clear semantics, a proper migration and a UI field. Tests are good and include a migration test. The main risk is that the test imports `migrate`, which may not be exported, and there is one stray whitespace edit in app.js.
